title: Spam & phishing triage
description: Decide what an inbound email is and what the mail gateway should do with it.
context:
From: "Chase Online Banking" <alerts@chase-secure-verify.com>
To: dave.morrison@acme-corp.com
Subject: URGENT: Your account has been temporarily suspended
Reply-To: support@chase-secure-verify.com
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 03:41:07 +0000
X-Originating-IP: 185.220.101.5
Authentication-Results: spf=fail; dkim=none; dmarc=fail

Dear Valued Customer,

We detected unusual sign-in activity on your account from an unrecognised device. To protect your funds, your online access has been temporarily suspended.

You must verify your identity within 24 hours or your account will be permanently closed:

  http://chase-secure-verify.com/restore?ref=8813-ACME

Please have your card number, expiry date and CVV ready to complete verification.

Thank you for banking with Chase.
Chase Security Team

safe_to_deliver.description: Whether this is a genuine message that can go straight to the inbox

impersonated_brand.description: The organisation the sender pretends to be, if any

sender_authenticated.description: Whether SPF, DKIM and DMARC checks passed for the sender domain

asks_for_credentials.description: Whether the email asks for passwords, card numbers or other secrets

urgency_pressure.description: How hard the email pushes the reader to act immediately

recommended_action.description: What the mail gateway should do
